transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um, hi. I guess I'm here because... I just have a really hard time staying on track with things. Like, I'll be working on an assignment or something, and then my phone buzzes, or I hear a song, or I just think of something else I want to do. And then I just completely forget what I was originally doing. It's just... really frustrating.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with staying focused and getting distracted? Have you had trouble like this since you were a kid, or did it start more recently?

Um... I'm not really sure about when I was younger. But I guess it's been causing real problems for... maybe a year and five months? 

That's when I stopped having structured school projects. I've been trying to build a freelance portfolio for UX and data visualization, and... yeah. It's mostly just been an issue since then.

When you're in situations where someone else is directing your attention—like in a meeting, watching a movie, or having a conversation with a friend—do you find it just as hard to stay focused, or is it mainly a problem when you're trying to work on your own?

Um... I guess it happens then, too. Like, I can sit down to read a research article, or... watch a UX tutorial. But after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the screen, and... I have no idea what I actually just took in. So... yeah. It's not just when I'm trying to make things.

You mentioned you're not sure about when you were younger. Let me ask more directly: when you were in elementary school or middle school, did teachers ever say you had trouble paying attention, or did you struggle to sit still and focus on schoolwork back then?

Um... yeah, I guess they did. I mean, in elementary school, my teachers used to write comments... saying I rushed through my worksheets, or lost track of directions. And... that I talked over other kids during group work. 

And at home, my parents usually had to sit right next to me while I did my homework. Because if they didn't, I would just... wander off. Or start doing something else before I actually finished it. So... yeah.
When you're sitting down to work or study, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, bouncing your leg, tapping your fingers, or feeling restless—like you need to move around or get up frequently?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, when I'm in portfolio reviews or... meetings, I usually end up bouncing my leg. Or... clicking a pen, twisting my rings around. Just... shifting in my seat a lot. I don't really notice I'm doing it until... well, until someone looks at me, I guess. So... yeah.

You mentioned teachers noticed these things in elementary school. Looking back, would you say you've had trouble with attention, focus, or staying still pretty much continuously from back then until now—or did things get better for a while and then come back?
Um... I don't really know. I guess... it's just always been like this. I don't remember it ever really stopping.

When you were younger—say in elementary or middle school—did you tend to blurt things out without thinking, or interrupt people a lot? Or would you rush into activities without waiting for instructions or your turn?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, even now, like... if we're brainstorming for a project, I'll just kind of... blurt out my idea. Or I'll start adding stuff to their Figma board before they're even done talking. I don't really mean to... I just get excited, I guess. But then later I realize I probably seemed really pushy. So... yeah, I've always kind of done that.

You mentioned these things have been happening since elementary school and are still going on now. How much have they actually affected your grades back then, or your work performance and relationships now? Like, has it caused real problems for you, or is it more just annoying?

Um... I guess it causes some problems. Like... I've lost a couple of small freelance things because of it. And I missed this portfolio competition once because... well, I just couldn't get it together to follow through on it. Um... some people I know, like friends or people I collaborate with... they like my ideas, but I think they're kind of hesitant to work with me sometimes. Just because... they're not sure I'll actually finish my part. So... yeah, it's not great.

When you were in elementary school, besides the rushing through worksheets and wandering off during homework that you mentioned—did you also have trouble organizing your materials, like losing papers or forgetting to bring things home from school?
Um... I don't really remember that specifically. I guess I might have lost things sometimes, but... I don't know for sure.

When you're in situations where you need to sit still for a while—like during a class, a meeting, or a long car ride—do you typically feel uncomfortable or restless, or do you manage okay as long as the activity itself is engaging?

Um... yeah, I guess I do get restless. Like... if I'm on a long Zoom call or something, and I just have to sit there... it's hard. I start getting this... uncomfortable pressure, I guess? Like I just need to get up and pace, or... do something with my hands. It just feels... uncomfortable.

Looking back to when you were around 5, 6, or 7 years old—before elementary school or early in elementary school—do you remember being described as hyperactive, or always on the go, or having a lot of energy that was hard to control? Or is the earliest you remember these issues being the rushing through worksheets and talking over kids in elementary school?
Um... I don't really know. I don't remember much from when I was that young. I just... remember the elementary school stuff.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with persistent inattention (difficulty sustaining focus, distractibility, mind wandering during reading/tutorials), hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms (fidgeting, leg bouncing, pen clicking, restlessness, blurting out ideas, interrupting), and impulsive behavior (starting tasks before instructions complete, rushing through work). Symptoms are reported since elementary school with continuous presence into adulthood, causing functional impairment in work performance (lost freelance opportunities, missed competitions) and social/collaborative relationships. While onset in childhood is confirmed through retrospective report of teacher comments and parental supervision needs, specific early childhood (before age 5-7) presentation is not clearly recalled. The symptom profile and functional impairment meet criteria for ADHD, Combined presentation.
